research_question: Can a compact raw-IQ encoder recover the sparse, beneficial P1n corrections that frozen MLCNN/handcrafted features could not identify, while retaining single-main inference?
teacher: seed-matched frozen P2c/P1n lower-score route, alpha=1

student.input: RMS-normalized raw I/Q plus frozen main probabilities and shared ISRJ physics features
student.architecture: four-stage depthwise-separable strided 1D encoder, global mean/max pooling, residual-logit and helpful-correction heads
student.loss: main-error-weighted truth BCE + 0.5 teacher-advantage-weighted soft BCE + 0.25 helpful-correction BCE

threshold_selection: training-selection identities only; maximize mean recall with every regime-power observed FPR<=0.08 and CP95<=0.15
next_if_pass: Freeze and benchmark parameters, FLOPs, memory and batch1/64 latency on untouched identities before end-to-end twelve-parameter confirmation.
stop_rule: If P3k fails, do not tune on development seed630000000; conclude that compact direct classification does not preserve the separated-waveform correction and move to training-time shared separation features.
